objective.primaryRule: two frozen procedures on identical populations (PROTOCOL.md §10), neither ordering an extra simulation: the ORIGINAL NL0 rule = the actual-profit role of the Q1-Q6 qualified members (highest centre net; ties: selection robust, lower centre DD, label) - the canonical reference method - and the experimental RA1, Assignment 2's code unchanged (screens S1 open-lot multiple <= 1.50, S2 open-lot share <= 25%, S3 worst per-lot MAE >= -$17,500, S4 selection worst-10% mean DD <= $35,000; then fewest failed screens, then the lowest occupancy within 5% of the best conservative training net, then ties), a co-equal experimental arm; RA2 (conservative net) a secondary ablation. Applied to Track I populations L (legacy cell), B (no entry-day book) and F (all 64 cells) at every cutoff, and at C24 also to N (Track N + the four incumbents) and U (F + N). Fold primaries = each Track I procedure's selection at C19, C21, C23.

risk.denominator: one fixed $100,000 principal budget (not peak account equity)

budget.notes: Distinct candidate proposals (centres; refinement moves apart), configured base / maximum: Track I broad 64 cells x 2 replicates x (512 screen + 2-6 islands x 256) = 131,072 / 262,144 per cutoff (524,288 / 1,048,576 over C19-C24); Track I stage-2 refinement <= 34 lanes x (<= 406 designs + 4-8 islands x 384) <= 66,028 / 118,252 per cutoff; Track N (C24) 16 family pairs x R_N (>= 4) replicates x (<= 656 designs + 4-8 x 384) = 140,288 / 238,592 at R_N = 4. Backend evaluations: job caps = the sum of the lanes' worst cases (41,000 per broad lane, 110,000 per refinement lane, 114,000 per informed lane), 700 per qualified member, 60,000 per fold evaluation, 60,000 for the validation: worst case about 46 M at R_N = 4, expected about 20-30 M (measured by the pilot, PROTOCOL.md section 8.4). Counted separately: screen, rung-1/2/3 and refinement centres and neighbours, qualification, folds, retries (runs.jsonl) and archive hits.

chronologicalConsequence: Standard 2.2.0 default: a Track I population x selector procedure whose sequential verdict fails or cannot be computed gives 'no chronological support: not a deployment-qualified candidate without the user's explicit decision'. Track N and U selections (C24 only) are labelled 'incumbent-informed; no independent chronological test' with the same consequence. Every Track I verdict is an independent chronological test (all three phenotypes searched fresh at every cutoff). 'No qualifying successor' is a valid outcome. Governance only: never a fitness term, ranking input or gate.

two frozen procedures (original, RA1) + RA2 ablation on identical populations L, B, F (Track I) and N, U (C24)
